I am a 51-year-old woman with no schooling, but I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for 20 years, and I know what works. My household has 7 mouths, and some of my family work in town, which brings in a little cash, but we still watch every yuan. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same land — that is what everyone here does. For wheat, I will rotary-till the soil in early October and sow an improved variety like my neighbors use. I will put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 50 kg — and topdress with half a bag of urea at jointing. That gives the crop enough food without breaking my purse. I will irrigate three times from my well: once before winter freeze, once at green-up, and once at grain filling. I will spray herbicide and insecticide two or three times if the bugs show up. For summer maize, there is no time to plow after wheat harvest — we plant straight into the stubble with hybrid seed from the shop. I will spread one bag of compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice, because maize drinks less than wheat if the summer rains come. I expect about 900 jin of wheat and 1,000 jin of maize per mu in a normal year, which keeps my family fed and leaves some grain to sell.
